clue.text: Perhaps May's second day, all very endless and black

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: without its end: both all and very lose their final letters here

parts.note: the two words taken as written, each then trimmed
the last letters of all and very, the ends that go
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A note about a woman called May's busy second day, everything very dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' serves both 'all' and 'very', giving AL and VER. The definition plays on May the name or the Prime Minister; here it is the verb may.
explanation.definitionFit: May, like can, must and should, is an auxiliary expressing possibility or permission, which grammar calls a modal.

clue.text: Stupid American encountered outside a dance

indicators.note: the word for encountered sits outside, around, the letter a

parts.note: met means encountered
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An American simpleton is met at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Meatball is US slang for a dull or stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: What comes in handy in golfing final

indicators.note: what comes in the following words is the run of letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Something handy in the closing stages of a golf tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying as an adjective means last or closing, as in the dying minutes of a match.

clue.text: Witnesses lone rooks flying

indicators.note: letters flying about are scattered and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Bystanders watch a solitary pair of rooks in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Lookers-on are spectators, people who watch an event without taking part.

clue.text: What makes one feel more able, say, to put up rent

definitions.text: What makes one feel more able

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the little word to is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: a rent is a tear, a rip

explanation.surface: Something to boost one's confidence when it's time to raise the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done to boost one's own sense of importance and capability.

clue.text: Conflict in unruly bar row involving ecstasy

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, involve, the drug's letter
unruly letters will not stay in order, so bar row is rearranged

parts.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A fight in a rowdy pub where a quarrel involves drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boer Wars were conflicts fought in South Africa between Britain and the Boer republics.

clue.text: Old heating unit bust after time

indicators.note: the bust's word comes after the letter for time

parts.note: a herm is a bust of Hermes on a square pillar

explanation.surface: The old radiator broke down over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a verb, broken; it is the sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: The therm was a former British unit of heat, used in gas billing, equal to 100,000 British thermal units.

clue.text: Show disapproval about tango and current music everyone plays

parts.note: to tut about something is to show disapproval of it
T is tango in the NATO alphabet
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Tutting at the tango and the latest tunes that everyone plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is a musical direction for all the performers to play together, or a passage so played.

clue.text: English spread out around Cape to destroy

indicators.note: the word for spread out goes around the letter for cape

parts.note: radiate means spread out from a centre
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: An English force fans out around a headland to wipe out the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out completely, to destroy root and branch.

clue.text: Some years supporting males in household

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting piece sits beneath the one it holds up

parts.note: men are males
an age is some years, a long period

explanation.surface: Several years spent propping up the men of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage is a domestic establishment, the members of a household.

clue.text: Friend's gone — I'm back inside

indicators.note: the turned letters go inside the word for gone

parts.note: ago means gone by, in the past

indicators.note: back means the letters of I'm are turned to read the other way

explanation.surface: A lament that a friend has left, and I have come back home.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English as a pal or mate.

clue.text: Risk damage when drilling patent bucket?

parts.note: patent means obvious, overt
to bucket, as in bucket down, is to rain hard

explanation.surface: Damage threatens when boring a hole into a patented bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drilling' suggests a power tool, but it is military drill or exercise; 'patent' and 'bucket' look like nouns, but are an adjective and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrain is to exercise so much that the body is harmed rather than improved.

clue.text: Bogey fault west of Paddington?

indicators.note: in an across answer, west of means to the left, so the fault comes first

parts.note: a bug is a fault, as in software
Paddington is the famous children's book bear

explanation.surface: A golf bogey and a fault on the line west of Paddington station.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is a London station with lines heading west, which suits the surface; here it is Paddington Bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogey, like a bugbear, is an object of dread or persistent annoyance.

clue.text: Annexe about to run into chalk ground

indicators.note: the annexe word goes about, around, the collision word

parts.note: a wing is an annexe to a building
to hit is to run into, collide with

explanation.surface: An extension about to encroach on chalky land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of'; 'about' is the containment and 'to run into' is HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiting is finely powdered chalk, used in whitewash and putty.

clue.text: Song at cricket ground such as Worcester and Oxford?

parts.note: Lord's is the London home of cricket
a spiritual is a religious folk song

explanation.surface: A song performed at a cricket ground, perhaps New Road Worcester or the Oxford Parks.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcester and Oxford host cricket, but here they are bishoprics: the Lords Spiritual are the bishops sitting in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bishops of Worcester and Oxford are examples of the senior clergy who sit in Britain's upper house.

clue.text: Concerned with a Conservative's regular turns

parts.note: re means about, concerning
per means a, as in so much per day
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A Conservative's routine performances on a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A repertory is the stock of pieces a performer or company regularly puts on, their usual acts.

clue.text: Roused to manoeuvres round King's royal emblem

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the king's letter
manoeuvres signals the letters of roused to being moved into a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: Troops roused to drill around the king's royal badge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor rose, combining the red and white roses, is the heraldic badge of England.

clue.text: What's part of beach life? Eros, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a starfish, a member of the zoological class Asteroidea found on beaches
second meaning: a minor planet, Eros being one orbiting near Earth

explanation.walkthrough: Eros suggests the god of love or the Piccadilly statue; it is also a near-Earth minor planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a starfish, as a zoological term, and a small rocky body orbiting the sun.

clue.text: One — and he spends freely — showing this?

definitions.text: One — and he spends freely — showing this?

indicators.note: letters arranged freely are not held to their order, so they are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone who spends without restraint displays a generous nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-handedness is generosity, the quality shown by anyone who lavishes money freely.

clue.text: Old still drink with doctor in charge

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An old distillery still, a drink and a doctor in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old still' reads as 'nevertheless old'; still is a noun, the distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is an antique distilling apparatus of two vessels joined by a tube.

clue.text: Figure month must lead to endless anguish

parts.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December

indicators.note: endless means the word for anguish loses its final letter

parts.note: agony is anguish

explanation.surface: A month that must bring an end to suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a plane shape with ten sides, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Minister's adviser regularly gets suit

parts.note: a spad is a special adviser to a UK government minister

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of gets is taken

explanation.surface: A minister's aide routinely gets a new suit of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAD, for special adviser, is British political jargon for a minister's party-appointed aide. 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of 'gets'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Post Office note about label showing cost of carriage

indicators.note: the note's letters go about, around, the label

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A post office slip on a label shows the delivery charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Portage is the charge made for transporting goods, the fee for carrying them.

clue.text: Dean not including verse in passage

indicators.note: not including means the letter for verse is left out

parts.note: a dean or dene is a valley

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean, leaving out a verse in a scripture passage.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean looks like a churchman; it is the old word for a narrow wooded valley.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow passage between buildings.

clue.text: Gradually destroy fuel element in reactor's heart

indicators.note: in places the element inside the word for the reactor's heart

parts.note: the core is the central part of a nuclear reactor
a fuel rod is an element of a nuclear reactor

explanation.surface: A fuel rod in a reactor core slowly wears away.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrode is to eat away little by little, as rust does to metal.

clue.text: Chamber piece too much involving two separate keys

indicators.note: the word for too much takes in, involves, the key letters at different points
separate says the two keys do not go in side by side but at different points

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, too much
C, the first of the two musical keys the clue asks for
E, the second musical key, going in apart from the first

explanation.surface: A chamber work that goes over the top by using two different keys.
explanation.walkthrough: The keys go in separately: C after the O and E after the first T.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a composition for eight instruments, a form of chamber music.

clue.text: Trouble holding double plastic bomb

indicators.note: the trouble word holds the rearranged letters within it

parts.note: to dog is to trouble, to plague

indicators.note: plastic means easily moulded, so the letters of double are reshaped

explanation.surface: Bother over a second batch of plastic explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic bomb' suggests plastic explosive, but 'plastic' here means reshaped. Dog as a verb means to trouble or plague.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodlebug was the wartime British nickname for the V-1 flying bomb.

clue.text: Best garden party?

parts.note: out, out of doors, is where a garden is
a do is a party

explanation.surface: The finest garden party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' reads as an adjective; it is the verb to beat. A garden party is an outdoor do.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass or beat them.

clue.text: Society dramatist of Elizabethan times in the manner of Fox

parts.note: John Lyly was an Elizabethan playwright, author of Euphues

explanation.surface: A high-society Elizabethan playwright, written in the style of a man called Fox.
explanation.walkthrough: Fox, capitalised, suggests a person; it is the cunning animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox is proverbially cunning, so acting like one is acting craftily.

clue.text: Happy to direct how refugees are often accommodated

parts.note: to con a ship is to direct its steering
refugees are often housed in tents, tented

explanation.surface: Pleased to oversee how refugees are housed in camps.
explanation.definitionFit: Contented means satisfied, at ease with one's situation.
